content: Dirithromycin is no longer available in the United States. If you are currently taking this medication, you should contact your doctor to discuss alternative treatment options. Dirithromycin is an antibiotic that is prescribed to treat specific bacterial infections, including bronchitis, pneumonia, and infections of the skin and throat. It is important to note that antibiotics like dirithromycin are ineffective against viral infections such as colds or the flu. In some cases, dirithromycin may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Dirithromycin is available as an enteric-coated tablet that should be taken orally. It is typically taken once daily for a duration of 7 to 14 days. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take dirithromycin exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. The tablets must be swallowed whole; do not chew, crush, or cut them. Take the medication with a full glass of water. Continue taking dirithromycin even if you feel better. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before taking dirithromycin, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to dirithromycin, azithromycin (Zithromax), clarithromycin (Biaxin), erythromycin, or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other antibiotics; anticoagulants (blood thinners) such as warfarin (Coumadin); astemizole (Hismanal); carbamazepine (Tegretol); cisapride (Propulsid); clozapine (Clozaril); cyclosporine (Neoral, Sandimmune); digoxin (Lanoxin); disopyramide (Norpace); ergotamine; felodipine (Plendil); lovastatin (Mevacor); phenytoin (Dilantin); pimozide (Orap); stomach medications such as antacids (Mylanta, Maalox), cimetidine (Tagamet), or ranitidine (Zantac); theophylline (Theo-Dur); triazolam (Halcion); and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had liver disease, yellowing of the skin or eyes, colitis, or stomach problems. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking dirithromycin, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking dirithromycin. Take dirithromycin with food or within one hour of eating. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Dirithromycin may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if any of the following symptoms are severe or persistent: upset stomach, diarrhea, vomiting, stomach cramps, mild skin rash, stomach pain, or headache. If you experience any of the following severe side effects, contact your doctor immediately: severe skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, wheezing, yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, pale stools, unusual tiredness, or vaginal infection. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store dirithromycin in the container it came in, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep the tablets at room temperature and away from excess heat and moisture (do not store in the bathroom). Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and the laboratory. Your doctor may order specific lab tests to monitor your response to dirithromycin. Do not share your medication with anyone else. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If you still have symptoms of infection after completing the course of dirithromycin, contact your doctor.
